issuing_body: State of Minnesota, Hennepin County District Court
title: State of Minnesota v. Mohamed Abdirashid Omarxeyd — Criminal Complaint
supports: The complaint alleges fraudulent billing by Guardian Home Health Services across PCA and several HCBS service types, including companion care, individualized home supports, homemaking, respite, and comprehensive community support.
The complaint explains that adult companion care includes assistance with daily living, errands, and social engagement, and that the UA modifier can indicate night supervision.
The complaint alleges ineligible overnight/sleep-hour billing, including more than $45,000 in IHS payments for services alleged to have been provided during a child's primary sleeping hours.
The complaint alleges more than $3.2 million was unlawfully received across the broader Guardian scheme; service-specific figures overlap and must not be summed into a new total.
does_not_support: The complaint is an allegation, not a conviction.
The total alleged loss cannot be allocated entirely to Adult Companion Services, IHS, or Night Supervision because multiple service types are involved.
A billing modifier or description of night supervision in the complaint does not establish a separate Night Supervision conspiracy or case family.
notes: High-value mixed-service primary filing for the 14-high-risk matrix. Use it to mark Adult Companion, IHS, and Night Supervision as having direct allegation coverage while preserving mixed-service scope.
